video.title: The Magic of Single-Foot Forehand Training

classification.reason: The coach demonstrates and explains single-foot forehand training drills and concepts using footage of a player and himself.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you train your forehand on one foot, and how does improper foot placement ruin your weight transfer and swing?
problem.definition: Players often fail to probe and place their loading foot behind the ball and deep enough into the corner, preventing proper body weight transfer and forcing an arm-reaching or curling stroke.
prerequisites: Open stance or semi-open forehand loading

symptoms.description: Reaching with the arm and curling the ball around during the swing instead of driving through.
Lack of forward weight transfer into the shot off the loading foot.
Upper body leaning and jumping around to compensate on almost every shot.
Ball feels like it never feels that good when struck.

causes.statement: The player is unable to press through the court with the loading foot toward the target.
The loading foot does not get positioned behind the ball and deep enough into the corner relative to the shot.
Inconsistent ball tracking and probing of the incoming ball into the body's optimal hitting spot.

angles.summary: The loading foot must be positioned behind the ball and deep in the corner so it can push back into and through the court for proper power and body unloading.
Contrasting an elite player who consistently probes to the perfect spot with the coach whose inconsistent probing requires constant upper-body lean adjustments.
Taking an identical swing regardless of foot positioning causes misses; players should adapt their body and finish when poorly probed rather than forcing a rigid swing.

solutions.summary: Perform forehand probing and hitting entirely on one foot (the loading foot) to punish poor positioning and train foot placement.
Get the loading foot out deep into the corner behind the ball and press it back into and through the court.
solutions.external_goal: Press the foot back towards the court into the crosscourt target.

solutions.summary: When caught in the wrong spot, focus intensely on the ball, swing through the ball you see, and adjust with the body rather than taking a blind identical swing.
solutions.external_goal: Focus on the ball and swing through it.
